fieldValues.title: Can an essay container declare its comments and references as children while agents still file into them (srs-web#634)?
fieldValues.decision_question: The owner ruled an essay must export whole from its own container, and that agents never write the essay but may file comments. The engine's write guard protects a container's whole closure, so declaring the comments and references containers as children of the essay container makes agent commenting fail. Which one gives way, or how do both hold?
fieldValues.context: Problem: srs-web#634 asks that the essay container declare its draft, Bin, comments and references containers (as childContainerIds) and its document-state record, so one slice export carries the whole essay. Built and tested against the real engine (branch feat/634-essay-exported-whole): once the comments container is a child of the essay container, an agent session's record_create into it is refused ('container ... is protected'), because the session write guard treats a guarded container's declared children as guarded. The existing test tests/essay-guard.wasm.test.ts fails for exactly this reason. Why it matters: two owner rulings collide. 'An essay can be exported without losing anything' (2026-10-28) needs the children declared; 'agents never write the essay text, they comment' (muDemocracy.org#226) needs agents to write into comments and references. Today the second holds and the first is met only by a separate snapshot bundle that leaves out threads. On 2026-11-12 the owner proposed nesting (vignette d289156c) and said 'I would prefer to move to an essay as a nested container set' (vignette eddae681): option E. Action needed: ratify E at the next session. Urgency: blocks srs-web#634 and the muSrs coherence cleanup; no data is at risk meanwhile.
fieldValues.friction: The collision came from putting the parent on the guarded container. The guard only flows down a closure, never up, so the parent belongs above the guarded containers, not on one of them.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: A: the engine guard stops at declared child containers by default, or a guard may list containers it leaves open (srs-rust change, then srs-web#634 builds as planned). B: keep children undeclared on the essay container and keep the snapshot bundle, widened to carry threads and vignettes (no core change; the owner's test 'export from its own container' is not met, the bundle stays). C: declare the children and accept that agents file comments through a different path, for example the essay package gives agents a record type outside the guarded closure (package change, more moving parts). D: do nothing. E (owner, 2026-11-12): an essay is a nested container set. One unguarded essay wrapper container, created with the essay, declares the paragraphs (essay) container, draft, Bin, comments, references and every thread container as childContainerIds, and holds the essay record and document-state as members. The guard keeps listing the paragraphs, draft and Bin containers, so comments and references sit outside every guarded closure and agents still file into them. Exporting the wrapper carries the whole essay; the snapshot bundle is retired. No engine change. Cost: the wrapper itself is unguarded (an agent could change its membership, never the essay text), and essay lookup moves up one level (lists, links, copyEssay find the wrapper). A remains available later if the wrapper's own membership needs protecting.
fieldValues.key_requirements: One slice export of the essay wrapper carries every record, relation, container and editor state; agents can still file a comment or reference; agents still cannot edit a paragraph body; no client-side reimplementation of engine semantics; membership declared, never derived.
fieldValues.decision_statement: Take E: an essay is a nested container set. A wrapper container created with the essay declares the essay's paragraphs, draft, Bin, comments, references and thread containers as children and holds the essay and document-state records; the write guard lists the paragraphs, draft and Bin containers only; the wrapper is what the essay exports; the snapshot bundle is retired. Existing essays are repaired by a script over the engine, never by hand. srs-web#634 is rewritten to this plan.
fieldValues.rationale: The owner's own design (vignettes d289156c, eddae681). It keeps both rulings with no engine change: the guard protects a closure downwards, so a parent above the guarded containers does not extend it. It replaces a derived, lazily built bundle with declared membership (RFC-034: membership is declared, never derived), and gives the essay one container that is the whole essay.
fieldValues.revisit_when: An agent edits the wrapper's membership in a way that loses part of an essay, or a second client needs the essay layout and finds the wrapper hard to locate; then take A as well, or move the layout into the essay package as a declared structure.
fieldValues.next_steps: 1. Ratify E at the next session. 2. Rewrite srs-web#634 to E: wrapper created by newEssay and copyEssay, threads declared as children when created, document-state as a member, refreshBundle and the snapshot container removed, essay lookup through the wrapper, a repair script for existing essays (muSrs c051c6a6 and others) and the end-to-end export test. 3. Drop the muDemocracy.org#395 allowlist entries once muSrs is repaired.
